item.title: The Murdaugh Family Murders
item.description:
Hey everyone, Cory here. Today we are looking at a case that completely consumed the South Carolina Lowcountry. The Murdaugh family was a legal dynasty, but everything started to unravel on a June night in 2021 when Maggie and Paul Murdaugh were found dead near the dog kennels of their hunting lodge.
Alex Murdaugh claimed he was visiting his mother who had dementia when the murders happened. But as investigators dug deeper, cellphone data and a crucial video started telling a very different story. We are diving into the timeline, the botched crime scene, and the massive trial that followed.

item.title: Elisa Lam and the Cecil Hotel
item.description:
I'm Cory, and this week on CrimeTimeSnacks we are looking at a case that completely took over the internet in 2013. Elisa Lam was a Canadian student traveling alone through California. When she vanished from a notorious Los Angeles hotel, the only clue left behind was a bizarre security video from an elevator that left millions of people guessing.
We will walk through Elisa's journey down the coast, her struggles with mental health, and her final known movements in downtown LA. The police had very little to go on, and the search of the massive hotel was restricted by legal limits, leaving her family desperate for answers.
Eventually, a gruesome discovery on the roof would answer where she went, but it only sparked more questions. We are going to dig into the actual facts of the investigation, the coroner's final conclusions, and how online sleuths built a massive mystery out of a tragic reality.

item.title: Murders in Moscow: The Plea
item.description:
Welcome back to CrimeTimeSnacks, I'm your host Cory. Today we are returning to Moscow, Idaho, to look at the legal aftermath of a tragedy that shook the nation. If you haven't heard our previous coverage of the devastating loss of Ethan, Madison, Xana, and Kaylee, you might want to start there. This time, we are focusing entirely on what happened after the arrest of Bryan Kohberger.
We will walk through the grueling pre-trial motions, the intense battles over DNA and cell-site evidence, and the sudden pivot to a plea agreement in the summer of 2025. It is a complex look at the justice system, the weight of capital punishment, and the legal maneuvering that followed the initial shock of the crimes.

item.title: The Menendez Brothers: The Parole Years
item.description:
Hey everyone, it's Cory. This time on CrimeTimeSnacks: what happened to Lyle and Erik Menendez after the verdict. Thirty years of appeals that went nowhere, the marriages inside prison walls, the TikTok generation that heard the abuse testimony differently, a letter found in a dresser, and a former Menudo member who came forward in 2023.
Then the part that is still moving: one district attorney who asked for resentencing and another who called their defense self-serving lies, the May 2025 ruling that cut their sentences to fifty years to life, the parole board that said no three months later, the judge who refused a new trial, and the early parole hearing now set for March 2027.
I covered the murders and the trials in an earlier episode, so this one tells 1989 once and spends its time on everything since.

item.title: The Interrogation of Chris Watts
item.description: Hey everyone, it's Cory. This time on CrimeTimeSnacks: the forty-eight hours in which Chris Watts's story came apart on camera. A friend who would not leave a doorstep, a patrol officer who noticed a husband was too calm, a neighbor's security camera, an FBI agent who held back his best evidence, a polygraph score of negative 18, and the way out that investigators offered him. Where the published accounts disagree, I say so. From the welfare check on August 13, 2018 to the oil site at 11 that night two days later, then the plea, the sentence, and the versions of the story he has told since.

item.title: The Disappearance of Gabby Petito
item.description:
Hey everyone, Cory here. This week on CrimeTimeSnacks, we are looking at a case that completely consumed the internet in the summer of 2021. Gabby Petito and her fiancé Brian Laundrie set out on a four-month van-life journey across the United States. They documented their travels on YouTube and Instagram, painting a picture of the perfect bohemian adventure among the national parks.
But the reality behind the camera was much darker. When Brian returned to his parents' home in Florida without Gabby, and then refused to speak to anyone about where she was, alarm bells rang nationwide. We are going to walk through their timeline, dive into the infamous Moab body-cam footage, and look at how this case changed the way police handle domestic disturbance calls.

item.title: Hunting the Golden State Killer
item.description:
For more than forty years, California was haunted by an elusive predator known across decades by different names: the Visalia Ransacker, the East Area Rapist, the Original Night Stalker, and ultimately, the Golden State Killer. Leaving behind dozens of violated homes, traumatized survivors, and shattered families, the attacker seemed to vanish into thin air by the mid-1980s, evading traditional police work and fingerprint databases alike.
In this episode, I walk you through how a predator who once wore a police badge managed to operate in the shadows, and how investigators revolutionized criminal forensics by using genetic genealogy to crack open the coldest trail in California history. We examine the timeline, the evidence, and the long road to unmasking an ordinary retiree living in a quiet suburban neighborhood.

item.title: Murders in Moscow
item.description: The Idaho student murders. On November 13, 2022, four University of Idaho students, Ethan Chapin, Madison Mogen, Xana Kernodle and Kaylee Goncalves, were killed in their off-campus rental home in Moscow, Idaho. This episode goes through what happened that night, the investigation that followed, and where the case against Bryan Kohberger stood in March 2025, before his plea.

item.title: Watts Family Murders
item.description: The Watts family murders occurred in August 2018 in Frederick, Colorado. Chris Watts, the father, killed his pregnant wife, Shanann, and their two young daughters, Bella and Celeste. The crime gained significant media attention due to its horrific nature and the subsequent investigation. Watts initially denied involvement but later confessed to the murders. He was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The case continues to be a source of fascination and discussion for true crime enthusiasts.

item.title: JonBenét Ramsey | The Facts 96-22 |Part 1
item.description: JonBenét Patricia Ramsey was murdered. That is the only certain thing about this case after 26 years. There is key evidence in this case, as well as more theories than there are people involved. I took weeks of research and broke it down into a two-part segment where I go over all the facts known in the case today, as well as some key suspects. I try to stay away from the theories that have little to no factual basis. Listen to the facts of the case and form your own opinion. item.title: JonBenét Ramsey Americas Child Beauty Queen
item.description: In Boulder, Colorado, just a day after Christmas in 1996, JonBenét Ramsey, a six-year-old child pageant star, was found dead in her basement. She had been beaten and strangled. That was hours after her parents, John and Patsy, reported her missing, and hours after her mom found a ransom note on a staircase in the house. Nobody has ever been convicted in this case, even 26 years later. This is the lead-in to a two-part special where we go back to Christmas 1996 and look again at all the facts in this case.

item.title: CrimeTimeSnacks: The Delphi Murder Case 2017
item.description: On February 14, 2017, the bodies of Abigail Williams (June 23, 2003 – February 13, 2017) and Liberty German (December 27, 2002 – February 13, 2017) were discovered near the Monon High Bridge Trail. The case has had no prominent suspects until recently. On October 28th police announced they had made an arrest in the case. A 50 year old Delphi Resident was arrested and charged with two felony counts of murder. Listen while we dive into the case starting over 5 years ago in on a beautiful hiking trail.
